html:
The Kishinev pogrom was an attack on the Jews of Kishinev, today Chișinău, at Easter 1903, in which 49 Jews were killed and hundreds of homes and shops wrecked over three days.

A local newspaper had spread the old blood libel. Police stood by. The town was then about half Jewish, part of the Pale of Settlement where the Russian Empire confined most of its Jews. Reports and photographs shocked opinion in Europe and America. The pogrom spurred Jewish self defence groups, mass emigration to the United States and support for Zionism. The poet Hayim Nahman Bialik wrote "In the City of Slaughter" about it. A second pogrom hit the city in 1905.
